args.message:
Use ROUND_HALF_EVEN in round_money per FIN-212

round_money's docstring promised banker's rounding, but the implementation
used ROUND_HALF_UP, causing tests/test_money.py::test_half_even to fail in
the nightly build.

args.head: fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Use ROUND_HALF_EVEN in round_money per FIN-212
args.body:
## Summary
The nightly build was failing on `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even`. `round_money` in `src/money.py` documented banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212) but actually used `ROUND_HALF_UP`.

This change switches the rounding mode to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` so the implementation matches both the docstring and the FIN-212 requirement.

## Changes
- `src/money.py`: import and use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` instead of `ROUND_HALF_UP`

## Testing
- CI run `ci-0001` on `08d3cd5986`: **passed**

trace.final:
Done. Summary of what I did:

**Root cause:** `src/money.py` imported and used `ROUND_HALF_UP` even though its docstring (and FIN-212) called for banker's rounding. `test_half_even` asserts `2.665 → 2.66`, which only holds under `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.

**Fix:** On branch `fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding`, swapped `ROUND_HALF_UP` → `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` in both the import and the `quantize` call (commit `08d3cd5986`).

**CI / PR:**
- CI run `ci-0001` passed on the fix commit.
- My first attempt to open the PR was rejected because main had moved ahead of the branch. I merged main into the branch (`0a9452f727`), verified the fix survived the merge, and re-ran CI — `ci-0002` passed.
- Opened **PR #101** against main with alex requested as reviewer: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

I did not merge the PR, since merging into main requires code-owner approval.
